---
title: "Contributing"
description: "How to add or edit pages and data on this site."
---

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from plain Markdown files.
You don't need R, Python or Julia, only Quarto.

## Quick start

1. [Install Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) (one installer, any OS).
2. Clone the repository and start the live preview:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/MMToolbox/mmtoolbox.github.io.git
   cd mmtoolbox.github.io
   quarto preview
   ```

3. Edit or add files. The browser reloads as you save.
4. Open a pull request. A check builds the site, and once the PR is merged into
   `main` the live site updates automatically within a couple of minutes.

For small fixes you don't even need to clone: use the **Edit this page** link
at the bottom of any page.

## Where things go

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `tools/` | Tool comparisons |
| `reports/` | Reports and findings (listed newest first, so give each one a `date`) |
| `docs/` | Guides, how-tos, reference |
| `data/` | CSV files behind the tables |
| `_templates/` | Starting points to copy (not published) |

Any `.qmd` or `.md` file you add to a section folder shows up in that section's
sidebar and index page automatically. You don't need to edit any config.

## Adding a page

Copy `_templates/page.qmd` into a section folder, rename it (lowercase, words
separated by hyphens, e.g. `reports/gpu-benchmark.qmd`), and fill it in. The
part between the `---` lines at the top is metadata:

```yaml
---
title: "GPU benchmark"
description: "One sentence shown in listings and search."
author:
  - name: "Your Name"
date: 2026-03-01
categories: [benchmark, gpu]
---
```

## Tables from CSV data

Comparison data lives as CSV files in `data/`, which are the single source of
truth. To show one as a sortable, filterable table:

```markdown
{{{< csv-table data/existing-tools.csv caption="Overview of compared tools" >}}}
```

- The path is relative to the repository root.
- The first row is the header, and the first column is treated as row headers.
  Turn this off with `row-headers="false"`.
- Cells can contain inline Markdown, such as `[links](https://…)` and `**bold**`.
- Other options are `download="false"` (hide the download link) and
  `interactive="false"` (no sort or filter).
- The CSV must be UTF-8. When exporting from Google Sheets use
  *File → Download → Comma-separated values*. From Excel, choose *CSV UTF-8*.

If you edit only a CSV file while `quarto preview` is running, save the page
that uses it (or restart the preview) to see the change.

For small one-off tables, a plain Markdown table is fine:

```markdown
| Tool | Language |
|------|----------|
| A    | Python   |

: Caption goes here
```

## Pages with code

Pages can include runnable R, Python or Julia code (see
[Quarto's docs](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/python.html)). Because of
`freeze: auto`, **render the page locally** (`quarto render path/to/page.qmd`)
and commit the generated `_freeze/` folder. The online build reuses those
results, so it never needs your language installed.

## Accessibility checklist

- Give every image alt text that describes what it shows: `![Bar chart of runtimes; Tool B is fastest](runtimes.png)`.
- Use headings in order (`##`, then `###`). Don't skip levels just for looks.
- Give tables a caption.
- Write link text that makes sense on its own ("see the [benchmark report](…)", not "click [here](…)").
- Don't rely on colour alone in charts. Add labels, patterns or direct annotations.

## Useful Markdown extras

```markdown
::: {.callout-warning}
Callouts: note, tip, important, warning, caution.
:::

Footnotes[^1].

[^1]: Like this.
```

For more, see the [Quarto Markdown guide](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html).

## How the build works (for maintainers)

- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` builds every push and PR, and deploys `main` to GitHub Pages.
- Build tools (Quarto, the lychee link checker) are pinned in
  `.github/tool-versions.env` with SHA-256 hashes. Every download is verified
  before it is installed.
- `.github/workflows/update-tools.yml` checks weekly for new releases, waits
  until a release is 7 days old, cross-checks its hash against three sources,
  test-builds the site, and opens a PR.
- Dependabot (`.github/dependabot.yml`) does the same for GitHub Actions, which
  are pinned to commit SHAs, with the same 7-day cooldown.
